chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: Showmanship and fast playing in early jazz
summary: Dance and Ramey agree showmanship spread jazz; flashy players like Charlie Parker today were once 'Flight of the Bumblebee' men.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, that was a big thing in those days. I mean, you know, that was one way, really, why I think jazz sort of spread as it did, because there was all this showmanship going on with it.
Yeah, it pays to advertise, and they took advantage of it, that's the best thing. commercialize.
Almost the earliest thing I can remember is sort of banjo players who played faster, you know, and drown everybody else out.

Yeah, exciting as it can be. And in those days -- for a guy were playing a lead instrument, and he could play "The Flight of the Bumblebee", he was the greatest. He was like Charlie Parker is today, you know. They'd say, man, that guy's playing "The Flight of the Bumblebee" on this saxophone, or on this trumpet. the and maybe playing all the wrong notes and everything, but he's exciting, you know.
